<head-word>כָּתָא, </head-word>
<head-word>כַּתָּא</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (כְּתַת) = h. סָפִיחַ, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>concretion, glebe</italic>, or 
<italic>alluvial mound</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—
<plural-form>Pl. כָּתִין, כַּתִּין,</plural-form> with suffix (כַּתָּהָא) כָּתָהָא. Targ. Job XIV, 19.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>after-crop</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—
<italic>Pl.</italic> as ab. Targ. Is. XXXVII, 30; Targ. II Kings XIX, 29. Targ. Lev. XXV, 5 (some ed. O. sing., v. Berl. Targ. O. II, p. 38). Ib. 11 כָּתָהָא ed. Berl. (oth. כַּתָּ'; Y. כַּאֲוָותָהָא, some ed. בַּ', perh. to be read: כַּתְוָותָהָא).—[Sabb. 110
<sup>b</sup> מכבתותא דמישרי, perh. מכַּתְוָותָא of the after-crop of valleys, v. בַּתְוָא].—כָּתְכָּתִין, כַּתְכַּתִּין 
<italic>third crop</italic>. Targ. Is. l. c.; Targ. II Kings l. c. (h. text שחיס, סחיש).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="K01339">
<head-word>כָּתַב</head-word>
<language-key> b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083">v. Ges.</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> H. Dict. s. v.) [
<italic>to join sign to sign</italic>,] 
<italic>to compose, write; to promise in writing, to will, assign, consign</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. 20
<sup>a</sup> וכ' ולא חקק it says (Deut. XXIV, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> ‘and he shall write’ but not engrave; Y. ib. II, 44
<sup>b</sup> top, v. 
<xref rid="K01358">כְּתִיבָה</xref>.</definition>
<notes> Macc. III, 6 (ref. to Lev. XIX, 28) עד שׁיִכְתּוֹב וכ' unless he writes (designs) and etches with ink, stibium or anything that marks; Sifra K’doshim, Par. 3, ch. VI, v. כְּתוֹבֶת.—Meg. 9
<sup>a</sup> כִּתְבוּ לי תורת וכ' write (translate) for me the Law &c. Ib. 7
<sup>a</sup> כִּתְבוּנִי בספר Ms. M. (ed. לדורות) write me down (record my deeds) in a book (Book of Esther). Ex. R. s. 47, beg. כְּתוֹב אתה write thou thyself. Sabb. XII, 3 הכּוֹתֵב וכ' he who writes two letters (on the Sabbath). Ib. 5 נתכוין לִכְתּוֹב ח"ית if he intended to write a Ḥeth.—Keth. IX, 1 הכּוֹתֵב לאשתו וכ' he who declares to his wife &c.; ib. 83
<sup>a</sup> תני ר' חייא האומר R. Ḥ. interpreted it, ‘he who says’ (verbally). Ib. 102
<sup>b</sup> מאי כּוֹתְבִין אומרים ‘they write’ (in the Mishnah) means merely they declare. Ib. V, 1 והיא כוֹתֶבֶת וכ' and she may write (a receipt), I have received &c.—Pes. 50
<sup>b</sup> כּוֹתְבֵי ספרים וכ' copyists of sacred books, or T’fillin &c. B. Bath. 14
<sup>b</sup> משה כ' ספרו וכ' Moses 
<pgbrk id="pg679" />is the author of his book, the chapter of Balaam, and the Book of Job; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. כָּתוּב, f. כְּתוּבָה; 
<plural-form>pl. כְּתוּבִים, כְּתוּבִין; כְּתוּבוֹת</plural-form>. Meg. 31
<sup>a</sup> דבר זה כ' בתורה וכ' this is written in the Law, and repeated in the Prophets &c. Ib. 7
<sup>a</sup> כבר כ' אני וכ' I am already recorded in the chronicles of &c. Y. Shek. VI, 49
<sup>d</sup> bot. כיצד היו הלוחות כ' how was the writing on the tablets arranged?—Gitt. 54
<sup>b</sup> כל ס"ת … כ' לשמן any scroll of the Law in which the Divine names are not written with full consciousness, v. שֵׁם; a. fr.—V. כָּתוּב.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִכְתָּב</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be written, be reduced to writing; to be written upon</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Meg. I, 8 הספרים נִכְתָּבִים בכל לשון the Biblical books may be written in (translated into) any language (v. ib. 9
<sup>a</sup>); ib. לא התירו שׁיִכָּתְבוּ וכ' they permitted them to be translated only into Greek. Ib. 7
<sup>a</sup> נאמרה לִיכָּתֵב was indited (by the divine spirit) for the purpose of being written (as a book); Yoma 29
<sup>a</sup> נתנה ליכתב (some ed. לִכְתּוֹב); a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִכְתִּיב</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to cause to be written </italic>or
<italic> recorded, to dictate, indite</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 22 כבר הִכְתַּבְתִּי לך וכ' I have already ordered to be written in the Law &c. Ruth R. to II, 14 אילו היה ראובן יודע שהק"בה מַכְתִּיב עליו וכ' if R. had known that the Lord would cause to be written about him (Gen. XXXVII, 21) &c.; a. fr.—Lev. R. s. 24 ג' פרשיות ה' לנו וכ' (Pesik. R. s. 15; Yalk. Ex. 307 כתכ) there are three sections that Moses indited for us in the Law.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to consign, enlist in the army, levy</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ex. R. s. 15 (מלך) ב"וד מַכְתִּיב לו וכ' a human king levies soldiers for himself, strong &c.; Tanḥ. Ḥayé 3 מסביב (corr. acc.). Cant. R. to II, 8, a. e. מַכְתֶּבֶת, v. טִירוֹנְיָא.—Part. pass. מוּכְתָּב 
<italic>recorded; levied</italic>. Kidd. IV, 5, v. אִסְטְרַטְיָא II.—Tosef. B. Bath. IV, 7; B. Bath. 92
<sup>b</sup>; Keth. 58
<sup>a</sup> מ' למלכות levied for royal service (comment.: 
<italic>sentenced to death</italic>); Kidd. 11
<sup>a</sup> נִכְתָּב.—Gen. R. s. 89 (Yalk. ib. 147 כתיב), v. סַקְרָרִין.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="K01340">
<head-word>כְּתַב, </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<head-word>כְּתוֹב</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same.</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> Targ. Deut. VI, 9 (v. Berl. Targ. O. II, p. 51). Ib. XXXI, 24. Targ. Josh. XVIII, 4; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. (כְּתוּב) כְּתִיב. Targ. Ex. XXXI, 18. Targ. O. Num. XI, 26 (Y. כתוביא); a. fr.—B. Kam. 88
<sup>a</sup> bot. כְּתַבְתִּינְהוּ לניכסי וכ' she willed her property to &c. Gitt. 20
<sup>a</sup> איהי קא כָתְבָה ליה she (the wife) had it written (at her expense). B. Bath. 168
<sup>b</sup> ולִיכְתּוֹב לן מר וכ' write for us another document (copy) in addition to this; a. v. fr.—Sabb. 115
<sup>b</sup> היכא דכְתִיבֵי תרגום וכ' when the books are written in Chaldaic or any other tongue (than Hebrew); a. fr.—Esp. (in arguments on Biblical texts) כ' or כ' רחמנא the Lord has written, 
<italic>the text reads</italic>. Pes. 21
<sup>b</sup> טעמא דכ'רחמנא וכ' this is so because the text reads לא יֵאָכֵל (passive voice), but if it did not read so &c. Ib. לִכְתּוֹב רחמנא וכ' it ought to read &c. Ber. 3
<sup>b</sup> א"ה לכתוב מהנשף וכ' if this were so (that נשף invariably means 
<italic>evening</italic>), it ought to read (I Sam. XXX, 17) מהנשף ועד הנשף; a. v. fr.—כְּתִיב 
<italic>it is written, it reads</italic> (used also in Hebr. diction). Ib. 13
<sup>b</sup> דִּכְ' לדבר בם for it says (Deut. XI, 19) ‘to 
<italic>speak</italic> thereof’; ה"נ הא כ' ודברת בם here, too, (in the first part of the Sh’ma) it says (VI, 7), ‘and thou shalt 
<italic>speak</italic> thereof’!—Meg. 10
<sup>b</sup> כ' הכא ויהי … וכ' התם ויהי here (Lev. IX, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>vayhi</italic> is used, and there (Gen. I, 5) 
<italic>vayhi</italic> is used.</definition>
<notes> Ib. והָכְ', והא כ' but does it not also read &c.?—Gen. R. s. 1 ומאי כ' אחריו and what do we read after this?—הדא הוא דכ', v. דָּא I.—Snh. 71
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. בעינן קרא כְּדִכְ' we must construe the Biblical text as it is written (literally, e.g. Mish. ib. VIII, 4 as an interpretation of Deut. XXI, 19); a. v. fr.—B. Kam. 66
<sup>a</sup> שינוי קונה כְּתִיבָה ותנינא כ' that a change of form of a stolen object gives possession (compelling the thief to restore in value) is written (intimated in the Biblical text) and has been taught in the Mishnah.—V. כְּתִיב.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpe.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִתְכְּתִיב, אִיכְּתִיב</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be written, recorded</italic> &c. Targ. Esth. I, 19.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Ps. XL, 8. Ib. LXXXVII, 6 דמִכָּתְבִין Ms. (ed. דמְכַתְּבִין 
<italic>Pa</italic>.); a. fr.—Meg. 7
<sup>a</sup> דאיבעי איכתיב וכ' (Ms. M. מאי דבעי כתיב, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note; Rashi: דאי בעי כתב) that which was liked was written down &c.; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="K01341">
<head-word>כְּתָב</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> preced.) 
<italic>writing, writ</italic>;
<italic> character.</italic></definition>
<notes> Ab. V, 6; Pes. 54
<sup>a</sup>; Sifré Deut. 355 (of things created in the last hour of the sixth day) הכתב והמִכְתָּב the art of writing and the writing on the tablets (Ex. XXXII, 16; Rashi to Pes. l. c. והמְכַתֵּב and the pencil); Mekh. B’shall., Vayassa, s. 5 only כתב. Ab. Zar. 10
<sup>a</sup> אין להם לא כ' ולא לשון they (the Romans) have neither (original) types nor language; Gitt. 80
<sup>a</sup> (of פרסיים!). Y. Meg. I, 71
<sup>b</sup> bot., v. אַשּׁוּרִי. Snh. 21
<sup>b</sup>; Meg. 8
<sup>b</sup> כ' עברי(ת), v. לִיבּוֹנָאָה. [Ib. עד שיכתבנו בכתב אשורית, strike out בכתב, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l., a. Meg. 9
<sup>a</sup>.]—תורה שֶׁבִּכְּ' written Law, opp. שבעל פה. Yoma 28
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—Meg. 18
<sup>b</sup> שלא מן הכ' without a written copy, from memory.—Pes. 21
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. דברים כִּכְתָבָן וכ' וכ' construe the Biblical words as they are written (Deut. XIV, 2</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>, to the resident stranger give it as a present, to the foreigner sell it.—כְּתַב יד 
<italic>signature</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. II, 3 sq.; a. fr.—Tosef. B. Kam. VII, 4 כ' היכר יד שלו.—Gen. R. s. 48 בכל מקום … הכ' רבה על הנקודה אתה דורש את הכ' וכ' wherever you find in the Biblical text the plain writing, i.e. the number of undotted letters in a word, prevailing over the number of the dotted, you must interpret the undotted (ignoring the dotted); where the dotted prevail, you must interpret the dotted, e.g. א̇לי̇ו̇ (Gen. XVIII, 9) read אַיּוֹ, where is he (Abraham)?; ib. s. 78; Cant. R. to VII, 5.—Tosef. Meg. IV (III), 41 (ref. to II Kings X, 27 מחראות) קורין אותו ככְתָבוֹ we read it as it is written (not as emended in the K’ri); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. כְּתָבִים, כְּתָבִין</plural-form>. Tanḥ Masé 1; Num. R. s. 23, beg. כ' רעים מן המלכות government papers containing orders of hard measures against the Jews. Esth. R. introd. כְּתָבָיו של מלך royal decrees. Ex. R. s. 20 עד שילמוד בני כ' (some ed. כתובין) until my son shall have studied documents; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="K01347">
<head-word>כָּתוּב</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (כָּתַב) 
<italic>Biblical verse, passage</italic>; הַכָּ' 
<italic>the Bible text</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥag. 18
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. במה הכ' מדבר of what does the text speak? Ib. הא לא מסרן הכ' אלא וכ' this proves that the Law intended to leave it to the discretion of the scholars to decide &c.—Pes. 3
<sup>a</sup> עקם הכ' שמנה וכ' the text made a circumlocution of eight letters (more than would have been required). Sifra introd., beg. בנין אב מכ' אחד a standard rule derived from one verse. Ib. end כ' אחד אומר וכ' one verse reads …, and another reads &c.; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. כְּתוּבִים, כְּתוּבִין</plural-form>. Sifra l. c. Snh. 45
<sup>b</sup>; Meïl. 11
<sup>b</sup>, v. לָמַד; a. fr.—[Ex. R. s. 20, v. כְּתָב.]—Esp. 
<italic>K’thubim, Hagiographa</italic>, the third part of the Bible. Keth. 50
<sup>a</sup> תורה נביאים וכ' (abbrev. תנ"ך) Pentateuch, Prophets and Hagiographa. B. Bath. 14
<sup>b</sup> סידרן של כ' וכ' the order of the books of the Hagiographa is: Ruth &c. Meg. 31
<sup>a</sup> ומשולש בכ' and for the third time intimated in the Hag.; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="K01348">
<head-word>כְּתוּבָא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes>—
<plural-form>Pl. כְּתוּבַיָּא, כְּתוּבֵי</plural-form>. Y. Ned. I, end, 37
<sup>a</sup> כקדושת כ' as sacred as the Biblical writings.—Esp. כְּתוּבֵי 
<italic>the Hagiographa</italic>.—Taan. 9
<sup>a</sup> מי איכא מידי דכתיבא בכ' וכ' is there anything written in the Hagiographa that is not intimated in the Law? B. Bath. 8
<sup>a</sup> עברת אדאורייתא ואדכ' … thou didst act against what is written in the Law, the Prophets and the Hagiographa. Keth. 106
<sup>b</sup> דאקרייך כ' לא וכ' he who taught thee the Hagiographa has not taught thee the Prophets; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="K01350">
<head-word>כְּתוּבָּה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced. wds.) 
<italic>writ, deed</italic>, esp. 
<italic>marriage contract</italic>, containing, among other things, the settlement of a certain amount due do the wife on her husband’s death or on being divorced; 
<italic>K’thubah, the wife’s settlement, widowhood</italic>.</definition>
<notes> [For the formula of the marriage contract, v. Keth. IV, 7—12.] Y. Yeb. XV, 14
<sup>d</sup> ב"ש עבדי כ' מדרש the Shammaites made the wording of the marriage contract the text for legal interpretation; מספר כְּתוּבָּתָהּ נלמוד וכ' from her marriage contract we learn (that she must receive her widowhood), for he writes to her &c. Ib. ר' מאיר עבד כ' וכ' R. M. made the formula of the deed of sale the text &c. (v. B. Mets. IX, 3).—Keth. I, 2 בתולה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ מאתים the widowhood of one marrying as a virgin is two hundred Zuz. Sabb. 14
<sup>b</sup>; 16
<sup>b</sup> שמעין … תיקן כ' לאשה Simon b. Shetaḥ introduced the written marriage contract (with the promise of a widowhood, in place of a deposit of the widowhood in securities); Keth. 82
<sup>b</sup> תיקן כל נכסיו אחראין לכתובתה ordained that the contract must contain a clause making all his landed estate a mortgage for her widowhood; Y. ib. VIII, 32
<sup>b</sup>, sq. Bab. ib. 10
<sup>a</sup> כְּתוּבַּת אשה מן התורה the widowhood endowment is intimated in the Torah. Ib. כתובת אלמנה אינה וכ' the endowment of one that married as a widow is not Biblical. Ib. 56

<sup>a</sup>, v. כָּרָה; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. כְּתִיבָן</plural-form>. Ned. 37
<sup>b</sup> קריין ולא כ' וכ' ולא קריין וכ' the rules about reading words not written (omitted in the text) and such as are written but not read (marked as superfluous) are a Mosaic (ancient, traditional)

<sup>b</sup> כ' היא אלא וכ' it is a writing, and what is needed to make it one word is bringing the two ends of the papers close together. Men. 34
<sup>a</sup> כ' הנוהגת לדורות a mode of writing used at all times (not stone inscriptions). Sabb. 103
<sup>a</sup> אין דרך כ' בכך this (using the left hand) is not the way of writing. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to וכ̇ת̇ב̇ת̇ם̇, Deut. VI, 9) שתהא כ̇ת̇יב̇ה ת̇מ̇ה that the writing must be perfect. Ib. 105
<sup>a</sup> (expl. א̇נ̇כ̇י̇, Ex. XX, 2, v. אָנֹכִי) א̇מירה נ̇עימה כ̇' י̇היבה a sweet proclamation, a writing, a gift; Yalk. Gen. 81. Gitt. 17
<sup>b</sup> משעת כ' ועד וכ' from the time the letter of divorce was written to the time of its delivery. Ib. 45
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Deut. VI, 8—9) כל שישנו בקשירה ישנו בכ' only he who is under the obligation of binding (the T’fillin on his arm), is fit for writing (the scrolls of the Law &c.). Keth. 102
<sup>b</sup> וקרי ליה לאמירה כ' and is ‘saying’ (verbal declaration) called ‘writing’ (consignment)?; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>the word</italic> כתב 
<italic>in Biblical texts</italic>.</definition>

<sup>a</sup> בין כ' לכ' וכ' if a person in reading the Sh’ma is in doubt as to whether he is at וכתבתם (of Deut. VI, 9) or at וכתבתם (of ib. XI, 20), he must go back to the first וכתבתם; Y. ib. II, 5
<sup>a</sup> כתיבת (corr. acc.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="L00009">

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (v. 
<xref rid="L00013">לַאי</xref>) 
<italic>no, not</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. II Deut. XXXIII, 3.—B. Kam. 60
<sup>a</sup> ואם ל' but if not, opp. אם יש.—Ḥull. 24
<sup>a</sup> הא ל' הכי but without it (if the text did not say so).—B. Kam. 10
<sup>a</sup> בל' איהו without him. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> אי ל' את but for thee (sitting on it); אי ל' אתון בדידי had you not been (sitting on it) with me. Ib. כחו ל' כגופו דמי his force (pressure by leaning) is not to be considered as an action equal to (sitting on it with) his body; a. v. fr.—אלא ל' but, must you not admit?, i.e. 
<italic>but to be sure</italic>, v. אֶלָּא. Ber. 2
<sup>b</sup>; a. v. fr.—מאי ל' what (does this mean)? Does it not (mean) that &c. Nidd. 5
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—Esp. (לַוו) לַאו m. (= לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה) 
<italic>a plain prohibitory law</italic>, the violation of which, in the absence of any severer punishment indicated in the Scripture, is punished with thirty-nine lashes (v. אַרְבָּעִים, s. v. אַרְבָּעָה). Men. 58
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. ל' שבכללות an implied prohibition, e. g. Lev. II, 11 (where כל implies any mixture of leaven or honey); Ex. XII, 9 (where אַל תאכלו refers to נָא, to מְבְשָּׁל, and implicitly to any preparation not through the action of fire). Ib. לא לַאוֵיה כל' וכ' the prohibition in this case is not a special one for itself as is the prohibition, ‘Thou shalt not muzzle’ (Deut. XXV, 4, which is preceded by the law regulating corporal punishment); Pes. 41
<sup>b</sup>.—ל' הבא מכלל עשה (v. כְּלָל) a prohibition derived by implication from a positive command, e. g. the law (Lev. I, 2) defining what animals are fit for the altar and indirectly excluding unclean animals. Zeb. 34
<sup>a</sup> … ל' … לוקין עליו the transgression of an implicit prohibition is punishable with lashes; ib. ל' … אין לוקין עליו is not punishable. Pes. l. c. ל' הבא מכלל עשה עשה a prohibition derived from a positive command is treated like a positive command (the neglect of which is not indictable); Ḥull. 81
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—ל' הניתק לעשה, v. נָתַק.—
<plural-form>Pl. לַאוִין</plural-form> (לַווִין). B. Mets. 111
<sup>a</sup> לעבור עליו בשני ל' to make the transgressor answerable for two acts.—חייבי ל' those guilty of transgressing a plain prohibitory law, punishable with lashes, contrad. to חייבי כריתות, ח' מיתות (v. חוּב h.).—Yeb. 10
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—Ch. pl. לַאוֵי. Ḥull. 80
<sup>b</sup>. Tem. 4
<sup>b</sup>.—[Tosef. Erub. XI (VIII), 23, v. לַאי.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>c</sup> top המלבנו ההן דמגפר וכ' under 
<italic>m’labben</italic> of the Mishnah is implied (any preparation for improving raw material, e. g.) he who pitches wood &c., v. אֶלִּיקָה. Ib. המיינטון חייב משום מְלַבֵּן he who cleanses amiant (v. אַמְיַינְטֹון) comes under the law forbidding polishing (on the Sabbath). Tosef. Ber. VII (VI), 2; Ber. 58
<sup>a</sup>; Y. ib. IX, 13
<sup>c</sup> top גזז ול' וכ' he (Adam) clipped (wool) and cleansed &c. Ab. Zar. V, 12 את שדרכו … לְלַבֵּן באור יְלַבֵּן וכ' such utensils as are ordinarily cleansed by being put in the fire (metal spits &c.) he must cleanse by fire.—Gen. R. s. 70 (play on לָבָן, Gen. XXIX, 5) do you know Him שהוא עתיד ללַבֵּן וכ' who will cleanse your sins to make them appear like snow (Is. I, 18)?; a. fr.—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. מְלוּבָּן 
<italic>finished, polished, refined</italic>. Nidd. 31
<sup>a</sup> (of an embryo) מל' ומזורז well-formed and of strong vitality; Snh. 70
<sup>b</sup>; Num. R. s. 10.—Ib. מל' ברשע finished (refined) in wickedness, v. אפדכסיס; Gen. R. s. 60; Ruth R. to II, 1; Yalk. Gen. 109.—Esp. a) 
<italic>to glaze tiles</italic>; 
<italic>to heat tiles</italic>. Bets. IV, 7 (33
<sup>a</sup>) אין מְלַבְּנִין את וכ' you must not heat (new) tiles (on Holy Days) for roasting on them; Y. ib. IV, end, 62
<sup>d</sup> מאן דאמר מלבנין בבדוקים he who says that you may heat tiles &c., refers to such as have been tested (to be sound under fire).—b) (of metal utensils, v. supra) 
<italic>to glow</italic>. Ḥull. 8
<sup>a</sup> ל' סכין וכ' if one made a knife glowing hot and cut with it; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְלוּבָּן, f. מְלוּבֶּנֶת. Y. Yeb. XVI, 15
<sup>c</sup> bot.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be glowed, heated</italic>.</definition>

<sup>b</sup> והאונין … משיִתְלַבְּנוּ bundles of flax are considered finished after they are baked; Sifra Thazr., Neg., Par. 5, ch. XIII.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִלְבִּין</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to grow white.</italic></definition>
<notes> Neg. I, 6 היו … והִלְבִּינוּ if the hair was black and turned white. Ib. IV, 4 עיקרן … וראשן מַלְבִּין if their roots are black and their tops white. Yoma VI, 8; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to whiten, cleanse</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Cant. R. to V, 11 להַלְבִּין כנף וכ' to make white one wing of a raven. Yoma. 39
<sup>b</sup> the Temple is called Lebanon שמַלְבִּין וכ' because it cleanses the sins &c.—Keth. 59
<sup>b</sup> הרוצה שיַלְבִּין את בתו he who desires to make his daughter white-complexioned (handsome); a. e.—Transf. (with פנים) 
<italic>to put to shame, expose.</italic> Ab. III, 11 המַלְבִּין פני וכ' he who exposes his fellowman to shame in public. B. Mets. 59
<sup>a</sup> נוח לו לאדם שיפיל … ואל יַלְבִּין וכ' man should rather have himself thrown into a furnace than put his neighbor to shame. Yalk. Deut. 938 אני מלבין פניהם I should put them to shame; (Pirké d’R. El. ch. XLIV מגלה, v. גָּלָה). B. Mets. 58
<sup>b</sup> כל המלבין … כאילו שופך דמים he who puts his neighbor to public shame is considered as if he shed blood; a. fr.—Y. Succ. V, 55
<sup>c</sup> bot. (play on נ̇ב̇ל̇) שמל̇ב̇ין כמה מיני זמר it shames (excels) many a musical instrument.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>
